extracted.intended_audience: Nominated Principal Applicants (and other applicants) to the CIHR Project Grant program; also peer reviewers and committee members
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on what the various Project Grant result documents mean and how applications are reviewed, scored, ranked (percent rank), and selected for funding (including streamlining, large grants, ties, equalization, Priority Announcements, and bridge grants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer assessments — required content (pre-meeting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each assigned reviewer provides: a summary of the application; a preliminary rating; a justification of the rating by stating the strengths and weaknesses of the application based on the evaluation criteria; top (competitive) or bottom (non-competitive) group selection; comments on the integration of sex and/or gender in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers provide these preliminary ratings and comments prior to the committee meeting. Note that reviewers are not bound by their preliminary ratings and can change them during the peer review committee meeting. See Project Grant peer review manual section 4.2.1: Conducting reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary rating (reviewer)
rubrics_metrics.description: A numerical preliminary rating assigned by each reviewer before the committee meeting to indicate their initial assessment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary ratings are used to prioritize applications for committee discussion (e.g., determining top 40%). They may differ from the final committee score because reviewers can revise ratings during the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigned reviewer justification (strengths and weaknesses per evaluation criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Justification of the preliminary rating that explicitly states the application's strengths and weaknesses grounded in the program's evaluation criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrative justification is provided in the reviewer assessment and helps applicants understand areas for improvement. See peer review manual for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top/bottom group selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers indicate whether the application belongs to the 'top (competitive)' or 'bottom (non-competitive)' group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This selection helps committees focus discussion and identify streamlining candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments on integration of sex and/or gender
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provide comments specifically addressing how sex and/or gender are integrated in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These comments are part of the reviewer assessment and inform scoring and feedback to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee consensus scoring process
rubrics_metrics.description: Following committee discussion, assigned reviewers are asked to reach a consensus score; then each committee member votes +/- 0.5 of the consensus score and these votes are averaged to calculate the application's final score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members also calibrate scores based on all applications reviewed by their committee. Preliminary ratings can differ from the committee's final scores. See peer review manual section 4.3: The Peer Review Committee Meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rating scale (0–4.9) and fundable threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications receive a final rating on a 0–4.9 scale. Applications with a final rating equal to or above 3.5 are considered fundable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundable applications (>= 3.5) are eligible to be funded across committees in order of percent rank until funds are exhausted. Streamlined applications are not eligible for full grant funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlining of applications (top 40% discussion rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Committees are asked to focus discussion on the top 40% of applications based on preliminary ratings; remaining applications are placed on a streamline candidate list and are removed from discussion only if no committee member objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streamlined applications are not discussed (unless objected to), do not receive committee votes, and their final rating is calculated as the average of the ratings from assigned reviewers. Streamlined applications may have a higher numeric rating but are systematically ranked behind discussed applications, which can lower their percent rank zone despite higher ratings. See peer review manual section 4.3.1: Streamlining of Applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent rank calculation and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application's standing within its assigned committee is converted into a percent rank to enable comparison across committees (percent rank stretches the scale so the first-ranked application in every committee receives 100%). Example formula: percent rank = 1 - (number_of_applications_ranked_higher / (committee_size - 1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percent rank allows CIHR to account for scoring differences and to fund an approximately proportional number of applications across committees. Example: rank 5/57 → percent rank = 1 - (4/56) = 92.9%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent rank zones (NOR/NOD reporting and funding interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: On the NOR/NOD applicants receive the percent rank zone (100–90%, 89.99–75%, 74.99–50%, 49.99–25%, 24.99–0%) rather than a specific ranking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percent rank zones help identify whether the application will be approved for funding, may be approved, or will not be approved prior to the final NOD. CIHR provides guidance: 90% and above = will be approved; 75%–89.99% = may be approved (could be funded because of overall success rate or equalization); below 75% = will not be approved for full grant funding. Indigenous Health Research and Priority Announcements may use different thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Recommendation (NOR) contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The NOR (uploaded before final decisions) contains the final rating, whether the application was discussed or streamlined, the percent rank zone within the committee, and the recommended average annual budget (before across-the-board cut).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOR is provided ~two weeks before the NOD to help applicants decide whether to resubmit; the NOR can also indicate issues of non-compliance with Acceptable Application Formats and PDF Attachments under 'Additional Information.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Decision (NOD) contents and 'not approved' rank
rubrics_metrics.description: The NOD (final document) contains the same information as the NOR plus final funding decisions and the final recommended budget for funded grants. For unsuccessful applications, the NOD now includes a 'not approved' rank showing relative placement to the funding cutoff (e.g., 'first not approved').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NOD represents the final funding decision. NODs also indicate non-compliance issues in 'Additional Information.' Applicants can contact support for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding decision sequencing (ranking, percent rank, 3.5 cutoff, budget exhaustion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding decisions follow: (1) rank applications within committee based on final ratings (0–4.9); (2) transform rankings to percent rank for cross-committee comparison; (3) fund applications with final rating >=3.5 across committees in order of percent rank until funds run out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streamlined applications are not eligible for full grant funding. CIHR monitors and may equalize success rates for certain groups as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large grants cohort and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Large grants (top ~2% of total grant amounts requested) have a specific funding envelope and, while reviewed in assigned committees, are combined into a separate cohort for funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A large grant can be highly ranked in its committee but still not funded if the large-grant envelope is exhausted; such applications may receive a bridge grant. Bridge grants are not counted in committee success rate calculations. The threshold for being a large grant fluctuates by competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie-handling policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more applications have identical final scores within a committee (a tie), CIHR's policy is to fund both or neither.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a tie falls at the committee cutoff and sufficient funds exist, both tied applications may be funded, increasing that committee's success rate compared to the initial cutoff-based number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equalization (monitoring and competition-level intervention)
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR monitors competition results to ensure the proportion of grants funded is at least equal to the proportion of applications submitted by certain groups (Early Career Researchers; female NPAs; French-language applicants; NPAs self-identifying as racialized; NPAs self-identifying as person with a disability) when there are sufficient numbers of scientifically meritorious applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility for equalization for racialized persons and persons with a disability is based on affirmative responses to specific questions in the Self-identification Questionnaire; female NPA equalization uses Canadian Common CV data. If proportions are unequal, CIHR creates a funding scenario and then funds additional applications from the under-represented group(s) with the next highest percent ranks across the competition until equalization is achieved. Interventions are done at the competition level and the NPA's second application in the same competition is not eligible for equalization if the NPA already has an application approved above the cut-off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indigenous Health Research (IHR) adjudication and budget commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications adjudicated by the Indigenous Health Research committee are handled as part of an iterative review process. CIHR has committed 4.6% of the Project Grant budget to support fundable IHR applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IHR applications may have lower thresholds for full grant funding and may be selected for iterative review; final decisions are on the NOD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Announcements (PAs) — eligibility and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: PAs are additional funding sources (usually institute/initiative priorities) for highly ranked applications aligned to specific research areas; they follow the same peer review process and funding-decision mechanics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once preliminary results are established, CIHR produces a list of applications that are: eligible for a PA; have a final score >=3.5; and are either below the Project Grant cut-off (for grants) or above the cut-off (for prizes/awards/supplemental funding). Eligible applications are assessed for relevance to the PA and funded in rank order as far as the budget allows. If an applicant is eligible for multiple PAs, the PA with the highest value is prioritized. Streamlined applications with a final score >=3.5 are eligible for PAs but discussed applications are prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bridge grants — allocation and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Bridge grants are allocated at the competition level based on percent rank after allocating funds to full grants and Priority Announcement grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streamlined applications with final score >=3.5 are eligible for bridge grants, but discussed applications are prioritized. CIHR aims to balance the number of full grants and bridge grants; numbers vary by competition and are not predetermined.

rubrics_metrics.name: NOR/NOD use to flag non-compliance with application formats/attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR uses the NOR and NOD to indicate any issues of non-compliance related to Acceptable Application Formats and PDF Attachments and/or allowable attachments identified during assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If non-compliance is identified, it will be listed under the 'Additional Information' section of the NOR or NOD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee size effects and calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee sizes typically range 20–80, which affects percent rank calculations (denominator impact) and can cause variability in committee success rates; committee members calibrate scores across applications they review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIHR cannot create equal-sized committees without forcing inappropriate expertise matches. Calibration and committee size contribute to inter-committee variability in success rates.
